newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, boosted by U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, boosted by U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Monday, boosted by strong U.S. Treasuries and hopes the U.S. Federal Reserve will hold rates steady.

"The market's rhythm is set to continue, nobody is expecting the Federal Reserve to raise rates," said a trader at a local bank. U.S. bonds benefitted from the January National Purchasing Managers Index which showed a lower-than-expected reading of 52.0.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/2 to 90-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.20 to 126.05.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting Open Market Committee is due to meet on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Another trader said the bond market was boosted by the strong performance of Argentine stocks which surged on upgrades of telecommunications companies.
Sentiment was also boosted early in the session by the bond market breaking through key resistance levels, most notably the FRB pushing past $90, said traders.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.15 percent from 5.05 percent.
